sights.address: 4900 Marie P DeBartolo Way, Santa Clara, CA 95054
sights.w: Home of the NFL's San Francisco 49ers and host of Super Bowl 50 and the 2026 Super Bowl LX, this open-air stadium also holds the 49ers Museum, an 20,000-sq-ft hall of trophies, memorabilia, and Hall of Fame exhibits.
sights.k: Stadium interior only by game/event ticket or scheduled tour. The 49ers Museum keeps separate hours (typically Fri-Sun) on non-event days; on gamedays it needs both a game and a museum ticket. Verify hours before visiting.

sights.n: SAP Center at San Jose (The Shark Tank)
sights.address: 525 W Santa Clara St, San Jose, CA 95113
sights.w: The 17,500-seat downtown arena nicknamed 'The Shark Tank,' home of the NHL's San Jose Sharks since 1993 and one of the busiest concert and event arenas in the country.
sights.k: Interior accessible only with a ticket to a Sharks game, concert, or event. No general tours.

sights.address: 1123 Coleman Ave, San Jose, CA 95110
sights.w: An 18,000-seat soccer-specific stadium beside the airport, home to MLS's San Jose Earthquakes and NWSL's Bay FC, known for its steep stands and the largest outdoor bar in North America.
sights.k: Match-day or event ticket required to enter; no regular public access otherwise.

sights.address: 1 Amphitheatre Pkwy, Mountain View, CA 94043
sights.w: Northern California's largest outdoor amphitheater, opened in 1986 by Bill Graham, seating about 22,500 between reserved seats and a big grass lawn, next to Shoreline Park by the bay.
sights.k: Open only for concerts, roughly May through October; entry by event ticket. Lawn seating is general admission.

sights.address: 14831 Pierce Rd, Saratoga, CA 95070
sights.w: A historic hilltop winery estate in the Saratoga foothills whose open-air amphitheater seats about 2,500 for an intimate summer concert series with sweeping views over Silicon Valley.
sights.k: Concert season runs spring through fall; entry by event ticket. Gates open ~2 hours before showtime; ~$20 per car parking.

sights.address: 4701 Great America Pkwy, Santa Clara, CA 95054
sights.w: A 100-acre amusement park opened in 1976 with roller coasters, a Boardwalk water area, and the landmark Carousel Columbia, celebrating its 50th season in 2026.
sights.k: Seasonal ride park; entry by ticket. Slated to close after the 2027 season (lease expires 2028) unless extended - still fully operating for now.

sights.address: 400 S First St, San Jose, CA 95113
sights.w: A 500-capacity live-music venue and nightclub in a former 1940s movie theater at the heart of the SoFA District, hosting touring rock, hip-hop, Latin, and electronic acts.
sights.k: Open for scheduled shows and club nights only; entry by ticket. Check the calendar before going.

sights.address: 377 Santana Row, San Jose, CA 95128
sights.w: Silicon Valley's premier open-air shopping and dining district on Stevens Creek Blvd, a European-styled neighborhood of ~50 shops, 30-plus restaurants, a boutique hotel, and a cinema, dubbed the 'Rodeo Drive of Silicon Valley.'
sights.k: Open-air district, free to stroll; individual shops and restaurants keep their own hours. Paid garages and street parking.

sights.address: 660 Stanford Shopping Center, Palo Alto, CA 94304
sights.w: An upscale open-air mall on El Camino Real at Sand Hill Road with 140-plus specialty stores from luxury brands to local favorites, adjoining the Stanford campus.
sights.k: Free to enter; store hours vary. Ample free parking.

sights.address: University Ave, Palo Alto, CA 94301
sights.w: The walkable spine of downtown Palo Alto, lined with boutiques, bookstores, cafes, art galleries, a cinema, and a dense run of restaurants a short walk from the Caltrain station.
sights.k: Public street district, free to explore; shops and restaurants set their own hours. Street parking is tight at peak times; use the public garages.

sights.address: Castro St, Mountain View, CA 94041
sights.w: Downtown Mountain View's pedestrian-friendly main street between Evelyn Ave and El Camino Real, packed with diverse restaurants, sidewalk cafes, beer gardens, boutiques, and a Sunday farmers' market.
sights.k: Public street district (100-300 blocks are a pedestrian mall); free to walk. Individual businesses keep their own hours.

sights.address: N Santa Cruz Ave, Los Gatos, CA 95030
sights.w: A picturesque four-to-five-block historic downtown along Santa Cruz Avenue with independent boutiques, art and cooking shops, fine dining, and turn-of-the-century architecture at the foot of the Santa Cruz Mountains.
sights.k: Public street district, free to stroll; shop and restaurant hours vary. A pleasant day-trip stop en route to Santa Cruz.

sights.address: 1875 S Bascom Ave, Campbell, CA 95008
sights.w: A relaxed open-air shopping, dining, and cinema center at Bascom and Campbell Avenues, named for the prune orchards it replaced and known for the landmark 1980s free-speech Supreme Court case that bears its name.
sights.k: Free to enter; store and restaurant hours vary. Just southwest of San Jose in Campbell.

sights.address: 387 S First St, San Jose, CA 95113
sights.w: Downtown San Jose's 'Creative District' (South of First Area), a cluster of galleries, theaters, live-music clubs, and the SoFA Market food hall, anchored by the monthly South First Fridays art walk.
sights.k: Public district, free to wander; the food hall and venues keep their own hours. South First Fridays runs the first Friday evening of each month.

sights.address: N 5th St & Jackson St, San Jose, CA 95112
sights.w: One of only three surviving historic Japantowns in the U.S., centered on Jackson and Fifth Streets, with the Japanese American Museum, family-run shops and restaurants, temples, and Empire Seven Studios murals.
sights.k: Public historic neighborhood, free to explore; museum, shops, and eateries keep their own hours. Also a strong food destination.

sights.n: Children's Discovery Museum of San Jose
sights.address: 180 Woz Way, San Jose, CA 95110
sights.w: A large purple hands-on children's museum on Woz Way (named for Apple's Steve Wozniak, its biggest founding donor), with interactive exhibits on water, art, science, and community for young families.
sights.k: Ticketed admission; check open days and hours before visiting. Near the convention center in downtown San Jose.

sights.address: 748 Story Rd, San Jose, CA 95112
sights.w: A family amusement park and accredited zoo in Kelley Park, mixing gentle rides, a puppet theater, and a Danny the Dragon ride with animal habitats for lemurs, jaguars, and more.
sights.k: Ticketed admission; typically closed some weekdays - check the calendar. Parking at 748 Story Rd or 1300 Senter Rd.

sights.address: 400 Beach St, Santa Cruz, CA 95060
sights.w: California's classic seaside amusement park on a mile of sandy beach, home to the 1924 Giant Dipper wooden coaster and 1911 Looff Carousel (both National Historic Landmarks), plus 40-plus rides, games, and food.
sights.k: Admission-free to enter the boardwalk; rides are pay-per-ride or wristband. Over the hill from the South Bay - a day-trip; hours are seasonal, so verify before going.

sights.n: Downtown San Jose Murals & Public Art
sights.address: 396 S First St, San Jose, CA 95113
sights.w: An outdoor gallery of 70-plus murals and installations produced by Empire Seven Studios and the SJ Walls festival, concentrated in the SoFA District and Japantown, including El Mac's 'Sophie Holding the World Together' at Discovery Meadow.
sights.k: Free, self-guided, viewable any time on public streets and walls. Cluster around S First St in SoFA; more in Japantown.

sights.address: N 2nd St & E St James St, San Jose, CA 95112
sights.w: A 6.8-acre downtown square laid out in 1848, ringed by the St. James Square Historic District's landmark courthouse, post office, and churches, and the site where President McKinley once spoke.
sights.k: Free public park, open daytime; a recent renovation has reopened it as a downtown green. Ringed by historic civic buildings.
